text:
anya: Heads-up — noticed a spike in "stitch failures" for streaming aggregates in EU yesterday, looks like late events are getting dropped instead of routing to replay. Dashboards show a 12% drop in hourly agg coverage.

mike: Ack. Do we know why they didn't flow to the backfill queue?

anya: Looks like routing policy kicked the default: `latency-first` and then quota-exhausted. Instead of falling back to the small on-demand replay lane, the system just returned 429 and dropped.

sam: Can we add a short-circuit that routes events older than N seconds into a "rescue_replay" path rather than failing? That would preserve UX and keep SLAs.

rachel: Agree in principle. Need to be careful about cost. If we auto-spill to replay we need a per-tenant spend cap and accounting in console.

anya: Proposal sketch:
- if event_age > 600s and primary_route==quota_exhausted -> route to `rescue_replay`
- `rescue_replay` has: `cap_usd` (default $25/day per tenant), `max_parallel_replays` (default 4), and `priority=low`.

mike: Love the guardrails. Can we implement it as a routing policy flag on the API: `spill_to_recompute=true|false` rather than mutating existing `routing` enum? Easier for rollouts.

sam: Minor naming bikeshed: `spill_to_recompute` vs `fallback_tier=rescue`. I prefer explicit `spill_to_recompute` for telemetry code readability.

rachel: Console UX needs: toggle, per-tenant cap input, and preflight cost estimate when enabling. Also show metric `rescue_spillover_count` and `rescue_cost_usd` in tenant view.

anya: Example API call for testing (dev env):
```
POST /v1/ingest?spill_to_recompute=true
Body: {"event_ts": 1710000000, "payload": {...}}
Headers: X-Tenant: acme
```
Response should return 202 and an assigned replay token when routed to rescue.

mike: Implementation plan:
- eng-platform: add `spill_to_recompute` flag to routing API -> canary in staging (me)
- eng-runtime: create `rescue_replay` queue with configurable caps (sam)
- console: add toggle + cost estimate (rachel)
- ops: instrument `rescue_spillover_count`, `rescue_stitch_fail_rate`, and add to alerts (opsbot)

rachel: For cost estimate, use 95th-percentile token-rate * avg_cost_per_token, plus fixed replay job overhead. We'll show an estimate and a warning.

anya: Also add backfill visibility on the per-route dashboard: show % of events spilled and average replay latency. That helps product debug impact.

sam: Quick question on quota semantics — if tenant hits global token quota, do we still let them spill into rescue? Might need an override so enterprise customers with reserved capacity can use rescue without consuming shared quota.

mike: Good call. Add `allow_reserved_spill` label on tenant config. Default false. Enterprise customers can opt-in.

opsbot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled: eng-platform/spill-flag v0.1 -> staging @ 2026-03-23T02:00Z, canary -> us-east region @ 2026-03-24T03:00Z. Automated smoke: ingest 1000 late events, expect <=1% drop.

rachel: We should add a console guard that shows "estimated daily cost if enabled" and require a confirm for non-admins.

anya: I'll draft a short spec and open a PR with the routing flag + quick unit tests. Mike, can you pick up the canary wiring? Sam, can you stand up the `rescue_replay` queue with the cap knobs? Rachel, file a small mock for the console panel. Ops, add a slack alert for >1000 rescue_replays/day for a tenant.

mike: Yep I'll own the canary.

sam: I'll prototype the queue + cap. Will need a tiny schema change: add `spill_policy` record on the tenant row (booleans + caps).

rachel: Filed a console task: https://redwood-internal/boards/console/3245 (mock + copy).

anya: One more – add an observability dashboard row:
- rescue_spillover_count (per-hour)
- rescue_success_rate
- avg_rescue_latency_ms
- rescue_cost_usd_per_tenant

mike: timeline: POC by EOW, staging canary next week, prod rollout after audit and cost guard.

sam: Quick test plan: synthetic late stream replay, verify aggregates rehydrate within 30m and dashboards recover.

rachel: UX note: show a small "replay in progress" badge on dashboards for the affected hourly tiles so product teams know data is recovering.

anya: Great. I'll open the spec thread and tag everyone.

opsbot: reminder: runbook link for replays: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/replay-runbook.md

mike: thanks team, moving forward. :thumbsup:
